html:
Maximilian I was an Austrian archduke made Emperor of Mexico in 1864 with the backing of the French army of Napoleon III. He was overthrown and shot by the Mexican republic in 1867.

Mexico had stopped paying its foreign debts, and France invaded in 1862. Though beaten at Puebla on 5 May 1862 by a Mexican army in which the young Porfirio Díaz fought, the day still celebrated as Cinco de Mayo, the French took Mexico City in 1863. Conservative Mexicans then offered the throne to Maximilian, a brother of the Austrian emperor. He lived in Chapultepec Castle with his wife Charlotte.

A liberal at heart, he kept many reforms of the republic, which angered his conservative backers. Benito Juárez's republican forces fought on. When the American Civil War ended, the United States pressed France to leave, and the French troops withdrew in 1867. Maximilian was captured at Querétaro and shot on 19 June 1867. Édouard Manet painted his execution.
sum: Maximilian I was an Austrian archduke made Emperor of Mexico in 1864 with the backing of the French army of Napoleon III. He was overthrown and shot by the Mexican republic in 1867.
